bull.b: Debt fell from roughly $714–732M in 2023–2024 to about $48M in 2026, sharply reducing debt-to-equity and financial risk. This materially improves flexibility to fund operations, absorb volatility, and retain more future cash for investment or deleveraging.

Healthcare Services reached a nearly $50M annual EBITDA run rate exiting FY26, while management expects margins to approximately double in FY27 and target low double-digit margins long term. This indicates a potentially durable profitability inflection as efficiency investments scale.

Four consecutive years of mid-20% Senior margins, including 26% in FY26, demonstrate resilience in SelectQuote’s agent-led distribution model. Sustained segment profitability provides an earnings foundation and may help offset volume pressure in Medicare-related markets.

bear.b: Management’s FY27 revenue midpoint is approximately 14% below FY26, indicating that current industry and strategic headwinds are expected to affect the business beyond a single quarter. Lower volume can constrain operating leverage and make sustained earnings growth harder.

Approximately $800M of debt and preferred equity carrying nearly 12% cost creates a substantial recurring cash burden. The roughly $45M annual interest expense can absorb operating gains, restrict reinvestment, and leave earnings sensitive to refinancing or funding-cost changes.

Despite positive operating and free cash flow in 2026, the multi-year record includes repeated negative operating cash flow and volatile free cash flow. This uneven conversion makes earnings quality less predictable and reduces confidence that reported profitability consistently funds the business.
